Kombucha on the truck since May 2024. Bottled, £3.50 a 330 ml bottle, sells best on hot Saturdays. Every batch gets a code like KB-0937 (year digit, week, batch), written on the masking tape on the jar and in this note.

## Where the SCOBY came from

Lucy at the Levenshulme market (the bao stall) gave me a SCOBY plus 300 ml of starter liquid on 4 May 2024. Thick as a pancake, about 1.5 cm. She'd had it going since 2021. Gave half to Tash's cousin in July, so it's spreading.

## Base brew

Per 4 L jar:

- 3.5 L filtered water
- 8 g loose black tea (Assam, Whittard), or 4 g black + 4 g green sencha
- 280 g white sugar, 70 g/L
- 400 ml starter liquid from the last batch (about 10%)
- the SCOBY

Steep tea in 1 L of water at 95°C for 8 min, dissolve the sugar, top up with the rest cold. Must be under 30°C before the SCOBY goes in or it cooks.

## First ferment

- muslin cloth and an elastic band on top, never a sealed lid
- 23 to 25°C, out of direct sun
- 7 to 10 days. Taste from day 6 with a straw from under the SCOBY
- target pH 3.0 to 3.2, sweetness half gone
- new baby SCOBY forms on the surface by day 5

## Second ferment and flavours

Bottle into 500 ml flip-tops, leave 3 cm headspace, add flavour, 2 to 3 days at room temp then fridge.

- ginger and lemon: 15 g grated ginger, 1 tbsp juice per bottle. Best seller.
- raspberry: 25 g crushed raspberries per bottle
- rhubarb from mum's allotment, cooked to a purée, 30 g per bottle
- hibiscus: 2 g dried flowers, gorgeous colour, nobody buys it

## Batch log (codes)

- KB-0919: first proper batch, 9 days, a bit vinegary
- KB-0927: ginger lemon, 8 days, perfect, 22 bottles
- KB-0933: raspberry, exploded one bottle in the van (see below)
- KB-0937: 50/50 black and green tea, 7 days at 25°C, the lightest, cleanest batch so far. This is the recipe now.
- KB-1004: winter batch, 14 days at 20°C, heat mat bought after this (£19)

## Bottles and pressure

KB-0933 went off like a cork gun on 17 Aug 2024 when the van hit 31°C. Rule since: burp bottles every 24 h during second ferment, and only use proper swing-top glass, never recycled screw-tops. One "test" plastic bottle per batch. When it's rock hard, everything goes in the fridge.

## The SCOBY hotel

Spare SCOBYs live in a 2 L jar with plain kombucha covering them, muslin on top, room temp. Top up with sweet tea monthly. If one goes black or grows fuzzy dry spots that's mould, bin it and the liquid. Brown stringy bits underneath are just yeast and are fine.

## Problems

- vinegar taste: over-fermented. Use it as starter liquid or salad dressing.
- flat: not enough sugar left at bottling, or the cap's not tight. Add 1 tsp sugar per bottle.
- fruit flies: tighter muslin, double layer
- Rob drinks it in the evening and then can't sleep. There's caffeine in it, about a third of a cup of tea per bottle, see [[Caffeine cutoff]].

## Kombucha vs kefir

The water kefir is faster, fizzier and has no tea, but needs feeding every 2 days, see [[Water kefir]]. Both sit on the same shelf in the commissary. Keep them apart, cross-contamination from the kefir grains turned KB-0951 cloudy. Same smell when it goes wrong as an old [[Yeast water starter]]: pure vinegar.
